Getting civilly married in Tbilisi, Georgia 🇬🇪, without an agency (August 2026)
Hi everyone. I’m writing to share our recent experience getting civilly married in Tbilisi, Georgia, without an agency. Notice that this was OUR experience, and it can be different for you. Please be respectful in the responses 🙏🏻

 1) Based on our personal experience, I recommend budgeting 2 days to complete the process. The day you present the documents and get married + one day to receive the apostille and the translation.

2) It is important to enter Georgia using the passport you want to use for the procedure, as that is the nationality/names/surnames that will appear on the marriage certificate, though it is also possible to add a second nationality to your certificate BUT it will be only mention on it but it is NOT possible to used another passport to do the process, only the one you crossed the border.

3) You need to buy a SIM card at the airport (or in the city center) because they will ask you for a local phone number to complete the application. We paid 35 GEL for one week unlimited internet package.

4) Start the process early. City Hall is open from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM. This will allow you to complete the entire process in one day in case something gets complicated or delayed. When we arrived at 9:00 AM there were very few people and everything moved quickly. However, by the afternoon, wait times exceeded 30 minutes.

5) Before heading to City Hall, you'll need to have your passports translated into Georgian and notarized. If you hold dual citizenship and want both nationalities on your certificate, both passports must be valid and translated. We actually got ours translated right outside City Hall that morning—it only took them about 40 minutes to be ready.

6) You also need to find 2 witnesses holding Georgian ID cards or two foreigners with their passports translated as well. In our case, we paid 200 GEL for the 2 witnesses at the same place where we translated our passports. There, they gave us a copy of their IDs, which we presented when starting the process.

 7) Go to City Hall, take a queue number, and submit all documents: passports with their Georgian translations, copies of the witnesses' IDs, and your local phone number.

8) Wait for an SMS text indicating whether all your documents are in order or if you need to return to clarify any issues. For us, the first notice to return to City Hall arrived after about 3 hours.

9) Once the documents are approved, you will receive a message, and at that point, you can return to City Hall with the two witnesses to sign the legal document.

10) Find a place to apostille and translate the marriage certificate (We translated to English/Spanish and French). They offered translations in several languages. Depending on how quickly you need it, it will be more or less expensive. It is possible to have it for the same day, next day, 4 days or one week later.

11) I recommend looking up reviews for the translation/apostille offices located near City Hall beforehand because, unfortunately, we had a poor experience with the one we found. They made multiple mistakes in the translation and in typing our names and registration numbers. So check everything several times to ensure there are no issues so you can return to Israel with all data correctly spelled and avoid future problems.

12) Be very patient and don't romanticize the process too much 😄. In our case, the bureaucracy felt heavy, and it wasn't romantic or special at all. It was just like going to the bank, haha!

And that's it! That was our experience. Even though it took longer than we expected and we had to spend the day at City Hall dealing with Georgia's poor customer service and bureaucracy, we made it happen!!!

P.D.: This was our first time getting married and we don't have children. You need to check if you need more documents in case you are divorced, widowed or have children.

👰🏽‍♀️💒🤵🏻
